text: Becky Biberstein Michael Green Frances Carr Tom Richhart Troy Cook Bobbie Jackson Kimberly Abney Sydnee Bradburn Leanne Lee Mike Holland Matt Norris and Michael Abercrombie This weekend November 14 15 the Church celebrates the Thirtythird Sunday in Ordinary Time Entering the last two weeks of our liturgical year our readings have a certain sense of finality to them Yet this finality is not meant to be seen as an ending but a new beginning Just as the old year gives way to the new so the Christian life is always pushing us towards that movement from the old man to the new From death to life th th Since you were faithful in small matters I will give you great responsibilities Come share your masters joy The reward Jesus describes is remarkable The master does not relieve the faithful servant of responsibility Instead he gives him more and that greater responsibility becomes a part of sharing in his joy Christian joy is not always found in having less asked of us Sometimes God draws us more deeply into his work by trusting us with more This also helps clarify what Christian littleness means Models such as St Thrse of Lisieux and Blessed Solanus Casey show the holiness of smallness Though that which was entrusted to them in this life seemed little in all worldly ways their lives have borne innumerable fruit over the past several decades Even the littlest of work entrusted to us by God can be multiplied within the hidden and humble lives that we live Others receive five talents and are called to bear fruit on a larger scale The third servants failure comes from somewhere else Out of fear I went off and buried your talent in the ground We should ask whether some of what we call humility or prudence is really fear of failure criticism or responsibility God does not ask everyone for the same fruit but he does ask us to be faithful with what we have received STENCILWORK AND RENOVATIONS The decorative artwork in the sanctuary has begun as signalled by the scaffolding that has gone up This week has focused on setup and preparatory work On Wednesday we reviewed the proposed colors for the stencils and I think the choices we came out with will beautifully match the sanctuary without overwhelming the space The stencilwork is meant to be background decoration that helps to highlight the woodworking in the sanctuary As mentioned last weekend stencilwork will continue around our weekday Mass and adoration schedule so that we can continue to use our sanctuary To allow for private prayer while painting is ongoing however weve once again turned our cry room into a makeshift chapel to reserve the Blessed Sacrament throughout the week This balance will ensure that we always have space for private prayer as renovation work continues In more general renovation news we have received a new Corrective Action Plan from Shawnee Construction As we requested this plan attempts to address the various concerns surrounding the millwork that were highlighted by our architectural team Though it will be a timeconsuming process the plan seems to be a step in the right direction The first phase is planning identifying what type of work or repair is needed in each area SECOND SESSION OF THE DIOCESAN SYNOD The second and final session of the diocesan synod will be this coming week meeting Friday and Saturday in Fort Wayne Please keep all delegates in prayer as we conclude this historic synod for our diocese the first synod in one hundred years After its completion we will look to Bishop Rhoades to highlight the pastoral priorities that he has identified from this process to help guide the direction of our diocese for the years to come In Christ Fr David Saturday November 14 400445 pm Confession 5:00pm Janis Lindzy Sunday
